checked_scope: Sharp known-prevalence and interval-prevalence bounds for the difference of squared coding losses with a common binary latent state and randomized arm assignment; binary-code closed form and finite-support algorithm.
checks: Expanded (R1-B)^2-(R0-B)^2 to d2-2(E[R1 B]-E[R0 B]); the B^2 term cancels only because the same latent state appears in both arms.
Rechecked the threshold-selection argument for minimum and maximum E[RB] at fixed prevalence, including fractional selection of a quantile atom and r=0,1.
Verified simultaneous endpoint attainment by conditionally independent report draws given one Bernoulli B; this preserves both report marginals and the common prevalence.
Verified compact prevalence optimization, continuity of quantile integrals, and interpolation by joint-law mixtures; bounded prevalence remains within its interval under mixtures.
Recomputed binary endpoints: p1-p0+2 min(p0,1-p1)=min(p0+p1,2-p0-p1), with the negative endpoint by swapping arms. The p0=p1=0 and 1/2 boundary examples agree.

Checked that finite marginal support makes all quantile-integral objectives piecewise linear with rational breakpoints and polynomial encoding cost. Prior attempt 2 really asserts an independently variable [-1,1] arm-loss set; the correction is appropriately confined to the common-state fixed-loss submodel.

Compared the final manuscript with the retained full prior manuscript(s), current mathematical problem statement and source-note binding; verified every recorded source digest used below. Approval is confined to the expressly checked mathematics.
